description:
Restore Your Mind | Slow Veena | Indian Classical

You gave everything away today. There's nothing left in the tank.

This isn't a racing mind — it's an empty one. The kind of tired that doesn't want stimulation or motivation, just something quiet to sit beside while the reserves slowly come back. The Veena is the right instrument for this. It's one of the oldest plucked strings in the world — soft, bell-like, sacred. Each note arrives gently and rings out, asking nothing of you.

This is 90 minutes of slow Veena in Raga Bhimpalasi — a tender afternoon raga of gentle longing and restoration. Its soft glides and unhurried phrasing feel less like music to listen to and more like something slowly being refilled in a mind that gave everything away. No percussion. No urgency. Just space to be empty for a while.

Let it play in the background and stop trying to get anything done. The refilling happens on its own.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Veena — ancient plucked string, soft bell-like sustain and gentle fretted glides
- Raga Bhimpalasi — tender afternoon raga, soft and restorative
- A quiet tanpura drone underneath — warm, grounding stillness
- No tabla, no percussion — nothing to track or follow
- 90 unbroken minutes at 432Hz tuning

⏱ Chapters
0:00    Settling — putting the day down
20:00   Soft and slow
45:00   Quiet refilling
70:00   Gentle restoration
85:00   Coming back

🧠 How to use:
Press play and stop doing. Let the Veena hold the space — you don't have to listen actively. Sit, lie down, or rest your eyes and let the empty feeling soften on its own.

⏱ Best for:
• Recovering after a long, draining day
• Resting a mentally over-spent, depleted mind
• Quiet evenings with nothing left to give
• Gentle background calm while you do nothing
• Slow restoration before sleep

production_spec.loop_seam: 10s in / 30s out, Suno extend 3-4x → loop in post to fill 90 min
production_spec.notes: Raga Bhimpalasi — tender afternoon raga. Sa Ga(komal) Ma Pa Ni(komal) Sa ascending; descending uses both Ni (komal and shuddh) — the two Ni and komal Ga give it its longing, restorative afternoon character. Komal Ga + komal Ni are the defining notes. NO tabla, no percussion — drained-mind lane needs space, not rhythm. Keep a warm tanpura drone underneath for grounding stillness. Alpha 10Hz binaural — restful-alert gentle restoration (not Theta/Delta sleep; this is recovery, not drift-off). LUFS -15 (gentle, restorative, slightly quieter than morning-active). Veena should sound plucked and bell-like with audible soft sustain and gentle fretted glides — not legato. EMOTIONAL TAG ROTATION: clip 1: 'like something slowly being refilled in a mind that gave everything away' · clip 2: 'soft and unhurried — the body finally allowed to be empty for a while' · clip 3: 'gentle bell-like notes ringing into stillness, asking nothing'. 90min = 3-4 Suno clips + loop extension.
